text:
Tristan Jarry has given Edmonton what it needed after a rough season: 11 starts, a 6-1-4 record, a .904 save percentage and 1.93 goals saved above expected (goals he stopped beyond what an average goalie would on those shots). Last season he was at -4.2 by our count. The Edmonton Journal's grades after the Nov. 15 win in Philadelphia read "Tristan Jarry steals another," and we credit that night at 3.99 on its own.

The shape of it is odd. He has been better than league average on medium and high danger shots and leaky on the easy ones: 10 goals on 269 low-danger shots, a .945 save rate against .962 for the league. Tighten that and the numbers get very good. His rebound control is a strength, with 8.8% of saves leading to another shot within three seconds (league 10.7%). He isn't carrying the whole load, with gaps between his last few starts, so every start still matters for his share of the net.
headline: Tristan Jarry is giving Edmonton saves
